rule: DagModel subqueries that filter by file location must also include bundle_name to correctly scope results across bundles
rationale: Since multi-bundle support was added, relative_fileloc alone is not unique across bundles; omitting bundle_name causes cross-bundle collisions in subquery joins

rule: Every HTTP status code a FastAPI route can actually raise must be declared in the route decorator's responses dict so the OpenAPI spec and generated clients include it
trigger: raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_4xx_...) inside a route whose @router decorator lacks that status code in responses={}
rationale: Undeclared status codes are invisible to the generated OpenAPI spec and openapi-ts client types, so callers have no type-safe way to handle those errors

evidence.excerpt: bulk endpoint decorator doesn't declare a 400 response; OpenAPI spec won't include this error case

rule: Multi-team validation error messages shared across connections, pools, and variables routes must be extracted into a single shared constant to avoid drift
trigger: identical multi_team error message string literal duplicated across two or more of connections.py / pools.py / variables.py
rationale: Duplicated literal error messages across endpoints drift over time and complicate future changes or translations; a single constant keeps all three routes in sync

evidence.excerpt: same literal error message duplicated across connections/pools/variables POST and PATCH

rule: Error messages that cite 'manually triggered' as the reason logical_date is None must also cover asset-triggered DAG runs, which equally have logical_date=None
trigger: error message string containing 'manually triggered' adjacent to a logical_date is None check on a DagRun
rationale: Asset-triggered DAG runs also have logical_date=None, so blaming only manual triggers is factually wrong and misleads operators

evidence.excerpt: an asset triggered Dag will also have logical_date is none; description is inaccurate

rule: Task-group pattern resolution logic invoked from a public API endpoint must reside inside the corresponding QueryTI filter class's to_orm method, not be inlined in the route handler
trigger: resolve_task_group_pattern_to_task_ids or equivalent task-group expansion code placed directly in a route function rather than in a QueryTI* subclass
rationale: Inlining the logic in the route bypasses the filter abstraction and breaks the guarantee that group filtering is always applied uniformly when QueryTITaskDisplayNamePatternSearch is used

evidence.excerpt: should live in QueryTITaskDisplayNamePatternSearch, subclass and implement custom to_orm method

rule: Do not use inspect to probe clear_task_instances function signatures at runtime; fix tests to pass expected arguments directly
trigger: inspect.signature or 'params' in params pattern used to conditionally pass arguments to clear_task_instances
rationale: Runtime signature introspection is fragile and unnecessary; the authoritative fix is updating the test to align with the real function signature

evidence.excerpt: we don't need inspect to check clear_task_instances; just fix the test

rule: Removing an existing public REST API query parameter is a breaking change; keep the old parameter and add the new one alongside it
trigger: diff removing a Query parameter (e.g. xcom_key) from a public route that previously exposed it
rationale: Callers depending on the old parameter break silently; both exact-match and pattern variants must coexist on the backend

evidence.excerpt: keep both xcom_key and xcom_key_pattern; removing xcom_key is a breaking change

rule: Logic used exclusively by a public API endpoint must not be placed under the ui/ service layer; move it to a common or public service module
trigger: service function inside api_fastapi/.../services/ui/ being imported or called from a public/ route
rationale: Services under ui/ are intended for UI-specific concerns; placing shared logic there creates an incorrect dependency and obscures the public API's service boundary

evidence.excerpt: used by the public API endpoint and should not live in a ui service

rule: Dashboard DAG state counts (active, failed, running, queued) must use a consistent semantic baseline—either all based on latest run or all based on any run—so counts cannot exceed the total number of DAGs
trigger: dashboard query mixing latest-run state with any-run state counts in the same response (e.g. failed uses latest_state while running/queued use any DagRun in that state)
rationale: Mixing semantics makes counts non-exclusive: a DAG with an old running run and a failed latest run appears in both buckets, causing the total to exceed the actual DAG count

evidence.excerpt: running/queued are 'any run in that state' but failed is 'latest run is failed'; counts no longer mutually exclusive

rule: Skip calling _serialize_xcoms() entirely when result_task_ids is an empty list; only call it when result_task_ids is None (DAG-authored default) or a non-empty list
trigger: await self._serialize_xcoms() called unconditionally or without checking result_task_ids == []
rationale: An empty result_task_ids signals the client explicitly opted out of results; querying XComs anyway wastes a DB round-trip and may leak data through an authorization-suppressed empty list path

evidence.excerpt: queries XComs for every finished run even when results not requested; guard when result_task_ids == []

rule: Execution-API JWT data models should expose only the scope field needed at the application layer; JWT validation fields (exp, aud, iss, nbf, iat) belong in the upstream JWTValidator, not in the application-level token model
trigger: Pydantic model for an execution-API token including JWT standard claims (exp, aud, iss, nbf, iat) alongside application-level fields like scope
rationale: JWT standard claims are consumed and validated by JWTValidator before the payload reaches application code; re-exposing them in the application model creates unnecessary coupling

evidence.excerpt: exp, aud only used at JWTValidator; only scope field needed in the application data model

rule: Regex-based query parameters in the execution API must use a _pattern suffix to match the public REST API naming convention
trigger: Annotated[str | None, Query(description='... pattern ...')] parameter whose name does not end in _pattern
rationale: The public REST API uses partition_key_pattern for regex filters; inconsistent naming on the execution API is misleading and suggests exact-match semantics to callers

evidence.excerpt: named partition_key but treats it as regex; inconsistent with public REST API's partition_key_pattern

rule: AssetEvent.extra filtering in execution-API routes must use _parse_extra_params() and JsonContains() rather than ad-hoc string splitting on '='
trigger: for item in extra: if '=' in item: k, v = item.split('=', 1) pattern applied to AssetEvent.extra
rationale: Ad-hoc splitting does not handle None (raises TypeError), misses multi-key payloads, and diverges from the established _parse_extra_params/JsonContains pattern used elsewhere in the same file

evidence.excerpt: extra defaults to None; unconditional iteration raises TypeError; reuse _parse_extra_params and JsonContains

rule: Execution-API asset resolvers must filter by AssetModel.active.has() when resolving an asset by name, to prevent workers from reading or writing state against removed assets
trigger: select(AssetModel.id).where(AssetModel.name == name) inside an execution-API route without .where(AssetModel.active.has())
rationale: An asset row persists in the DB after removal from its DAG but loses its asset_active partner; resolving such a row lets workers operate against a logically inactive asset

evidence.excerpt: other execution-API routes filter by AssetModel.active.has(); omitting it lets removed assets resolve

rule: JWT generation for the execution token must occur inside the same try/except block that commits the TaskInstance state transition, so a token-generation failure does not leave a TI committed as running without a token
trigger: execution_token = generator.generate(...) or response.headers['X-Execution-Token'] = ... placed after the try/except that commits TI state
rationale: If JWT generation fails after TI state is committed the task instance is stuck in RUNNING with no way for the worker to authenticate, creating an unrecoverable inconsistency

evidence.excerpt: if generate raises, API returns 500 but TI was already committed as running; move into try/except

rule: OpenAPI HTTP exception description strings within the same route file must consistently either all end with a period or none do
trigger: create_openapi_http_exception_doc([...]) call where some description strings end with '.' and others do not within the same file
rationale: Inconsistent punctuation in generated OpenAPI descriptions creates visual noise in generated docs and client stubs; Airflow reviewers enforce uniformity within a file

evidence.excerpt: half descriptions end with '.' and half don't in the same file; pick one consistent with default error responses

rule: Do not use hasattr(state, 'value') guards on Airflow state enum types; all TerminalTIState, TerminalStateNonSuccess, and TaskInstanceState values always have .value
trigger: hasattr(some_state, 'value') pattern used with a variable typed as TerminalTIState, TerminalStateNonSuccess, or TaskInstanceState
rationale: These are str enums in Airflow and always have .value; the guard is dead code that obscures intent and can mask incorrect type annotations

evidence.excerpt: hasattr guards unnecessary; TerminalTIState/TaskInstanceState always have .value; simplify to str() comparison

rule: Remove TODO comments that document conclusions of already-completed investigations; if the conclusion is 'no easy way to achieve this', delete the comment rather than leaving it in code
trigger: # TODO: comment in execution_api routes where the investigation has already concluded it is infeasible
rationale: Stale TODO comments clutter the code and suggest pending work that will never happen; reviewers explicitly request removal when investigation is complete

evidence.excerpt: no easy way to achieve it based on current airflow design; let's remove the TODO
